messages:
alyssa: Heads-up: wrote a short follow-up to the sampling vs enrichment attribution RFC. TL;DR: we can push tenant attribution earlier (edge headers) or rely on late enrichment. want quick check on ops/dev tradeoffs.

priya: Can you paste the two field shapes? curious about backwards compat and cardinality.

alyssa: Sure — quick sketch:
```
Option A: pre-enrich headers
  billing_key: <string>      # small, forced-by-ingest
  tenant_tags: [str]        # low-cardinality

Option B: post-enrich envelope
  billing_key: <string>
  svc_annotations: {..}     # high-cardinality, added later
```

sam: Big ops note: pre-enrich means we can cheaply route and charge at edge, but if we screw up header shape we need migration. Also sampling decisions at edge mean lost context for late enrichment.

devon: Analytics view: post-enrich gives richer attribution (segment + feature flags) -> better accuracy for billing -> but costs more ingest and storage.

kai: Infra idea: middle-ground? accept pre-enrich `billing_key` for billing, but capture a lightweight opaque `envelope_id` on ingest so enrich can attach more attributes later and we reconcile. Reconciliation window question.

priya: Agree. Reconciliation needs deterministic merge key. Propose: ingest generates `envelope_id` (uuid4) and includes it in both fast path and enrichment path. enrichment emits reconciliation delta events keyed by envelope_id.

alyssa: Sounds doable. open questions: 1) reconciliation latency (SLO), 2) how to surface reconciled vs provisional usage in console, 3) migration path for customers without headers.

sam: We should also add a soft-fail: if `billing_key` missing, mark as `unassigned` and route to low-cost retention. Avoid mis-billing.

ingest-bot: Ingest pipeline: job 4832 scheduled to add envelope_id header on 2026-04-02. @sam @kai

devon: I'll draft the reconciliation outline + UI indicators. Will post a short doc.

alyssa: :thumbsup: let's sync Wed 10am EST. I'll update the RFC with `envelope_id` pattern and minimal header schema.
